terra.problem: It gives a reason for Elisha naming Jehu's relatives that the text does not state.
The text does not mention a table or say that the door closed before anyone heard the message.
The text says the commanders were sitting together, not that the prophet was in the middle of the army or that a camp full of soldiers was there.
It states as fact that Jehu did not see the news coming; the text does not say that.
The claim about judges as earlier leaders needs a reference outside this passage.
The passages do not establish that the oil used for Jehu was the same oil used to anoint priests.
The closing line reverses Elisha's instructions: the prophet is to pour the oil and then speak, not say it and then pour it.
The text does not mention a table or say that every commander wondered whether the message was for him.
The text says the commanders were sitting together, but does not mention a table.
The claim that Ahab was king before his son Joram is outside this passage and needs a reference.
The claim that Jezebel was Ahab's wife is outside this passage and needs a reference.
The text does not say the servants saw the prophet dash in and out or that this was why they called him a madman.
The takeout-menu joke draws on the drawer backstory without explaining that the menus were in the drawer.
The text does not say what the servants saw or establish that this was their assessment of the prophet's behavior.
The joke suggests a second 'Tell us now,' but the text records the servants saying it once.
The reference to battles at Ramoth-gilead draws on events outside this passage without a reference.
The text does not say there were no speeches first or that nobody went looking for a rug.
The passage does not say that only a few minutes passed.
